scope: Proposition 5.3 (Empirical row law and force normalization) of the manuscript “Microscopic jamming in the negative spherical perceptron” (preprints/Microscopic-jamming-in-the-negative-spherical-perceptron-September-24-2026/Microscopic-jamming-in-the-negative-spherical-perceptron-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 222 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8d94e973e689e60b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 49. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For either the Gaussian law or any mixture in Theorem 5.1, at fixed β > 0 and 0 < α ≤ B0, LN converges weakly in probability to µβ,α. This measure is atomless, assigns positive mass to (−∞, −1), and has finite moments of its negative part. The gap and normalized-force observables in the problem have inner N → ∞ limits at every fixed argument, and those limits agree for all these entry laws.
